papers.title: mTOR signalling, not clock gene rhythms, organises daily physiology
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that mTOR is a major clock output pathway required for most daily variation in mammalian physiology, with PERIOD2 interacting directly with mTORC1. Acute mTOR inhibition abolishes functional rhythms in cells and most daily liver physiology, while preserving sleep/wake cycles, and shows evolutionary conservation as a circadian effector across species.

papers.title: Acute sleep deprivation induces ECM-associated transcription and MMP12-sensitive perivascular remodeling.
papers.summary: Integrated re-analysis of three 6-h sleep deprivation transcriptomic datasets with tracer, imaging, electron microscopy, and pharmacological experiments in mice, showing acute SD increases ECM-related transcription and remodels the perivascular interface. MMP12 inhibition (MMP408) attenuated tracer redistribution and perivascular widening, linking an MMP12-sensitive component to SD-induced structural plasticity without restoring the endothelial-basement membrane complex.

papers.title: Flavonoid chronotherapy normalizes circadian dynamics and sleep architecture in mice with painful nerve injury
papers.summary: In PER2::LUC mice with spared nerve injury, the flavonoids nobiletin and tangeretin alleviated dynamic hypersensitivity on post-surgical day 14 and restored SNI-increased Per2 rhythm amplitude in dorsal root ganglia to pre-surgical levels. Tangeretin additionally alleviated SNI-induced disturbances in NREM sleep and wakefulness, supporting flavonoid chronotherapy targeting circadian disruption in neuropathic pain.

papers.title: AnySleep: a channel-agnostic deep learning system for high-resolution sleep staging in multi-center cohorts.
papers.summary: Developed AnySleep, a channel-agnostic deep neural network trained and validated on over 20,000 overnight recordings from 28 datasets that scores sleep from EEG or EOG at adjustable temporal resolution. It attains state-of-the-art 30-s epoch performance, remains strong with single EEG derivations or EOG alone, and at sub-30-s resolution captures short wake intrusions and improves prediction of obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy type 1, and insomnia.

papers.title: Characterization of Sleep, Spectral, and Epileptiform Activity in Individuals Aged 8-27 Years with SYNGAP1-Related Disorder Using an at-Home Dry EEG Headband
papers.summary: Using an at-home dry-electrode EEG headband in a decentralized protocol, the study collected 180 recordings from 23 participants with SYNGAP1-related disorder, showing increased wake after sleep onset, reduced sleep efficiency, altered sleep-stage distribution, and interictal epileptiform discharges in 22 of 23 participants. It also reproduced awake spectral abnormalities and revealed sleep-stage-dependent spectral biomarker dynamics.

papers.title: Capturing the rhythm: methodological choices shape inference from circadian activity data
papers.summary: Used 24-h activity data from individual male and female Drosophila melanogaster across five populations to systematically compare model classes, sampling strategies, and temporal bin sizes. Generalized additive mixed models on high-frequency continuous data with 1-5 minute bins gave the most robust inference, though appropriately matched cosinor/polynomial GLMs, targeted snapshot sampling, and bins under one hour yielded similar biological conclusions.

papers.title: Measuring Sleep at Home in Adolescents With Autism Using EEG Headbands: Protocol for a Remote Study.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a remote study using wearable EEG headbands to monitor sleep at home in adolescents with autism (n=77) and typically developing peers (n=65), including a personalized 2-week desensitization protocol for sensory sensitivities. 146 participants completed the study with at least one usable night of sleep data, enabling tests of whether thalamocortical circuit dysfunction underlies poor sleep in ASD.

papers.title: An automated EEG-ECG framework for CAP-HRV analysis: enabling brain-heart coupling studies in sleep disorders.
papers.summary: Presents an open-source MATLAB framework integrating rule-based CAP A1 detection during slow-wave sleep with HRV feature extraction via PhysioZoo/mhrv in a single time-synchronized EEG-ECG pipeline. A worked example on the OSAD+ subgroup (n=18) and a descriptive healthy-sleep A1-event HRV reference from the CAP Sleep Database (15 controls, 785 A1 epochs) demonstrate synchronized CAP-HRV output; CAP A1 detection is not yet benchmarked against expert manual scoring.

papers.title: Differential circadian time modulates of dentate gyrus and CA1 excitation-inhibition balance and seizure threshold.
papers.summary: Using vEEG, optogenetic seizure induction, mRNA sequencing, and patch-clamp in male ICR mice, this study found divergent circadian regulation of seizure thresholds between dentate gyrus and CA1, with the CA1 diurnal-nocturnal pattern matching systemic pilocarpine-induced seizures. Circadian cycles differentially modulated excitatory/inhibitory synaptic transmission and intrinsic excitability of DG and CA1 principal neurons.

papers.title: Motor memory consolidation during sleep after stroke: the rehabilitation timing hypothesis.
papers.summary: Reviews mechanistic, preclinical, and clinical evidence for a rehabilitation timing hypothesis in which motor therapy scheduled near sleep enhances sleep-dependent motor memory consolidation after stroke. Identifies sleep spindles nested in NREM slow oscillations as a principal substrate disrupted by stroke, and concludes that direct stroke evidence is lacking and trials testing therapy timing as an independent variable are needed.

papers.title: Sex differences in associations between sleep architecture and CBC-derived immune cell indices in MDD with comorbid insomnia.
papers.summary: In 126 MDD patients with comorbid insomnia, this study examined sex-specific associations between polysomnography sleep architecture and CBC-derived immune cell indices. Significant immune cell count correlations were found primarily in males (e.g., lymphocyte count with total sleep time and REM measures), while no significant correlations remained in females.

papers.title: Circadian-melatonin signaling in general anesthesia: molecular mechanisms and perioperative implications.
papers.summary: Reviews how anesthetic agents, surgical stress, and the perioperative environment interact with suprachiasmatic, peripheral clock, and pineal melatonin signaling, including proposed clock-repression and metabolic mechanisms largely unconfirmed in humans. Concludes preoperative melatonin anxiolysis is the best-supported indication, while evidence for postoperative sleep, analgesia, delirium prevention, and organ protection remains heterogeneous and of low certainty.

papers.title: Validation of the Telephone MoCA in iRBD and Parkinson's Disease with Conversion to the Standard MoCA.
papers.summary: In 137 OPDC cohort participants (controls, iRBD, PD), T-MoCA and face-to-face MoCA-22 scores were statistically equivalent with minimal bias, though concordance was moderate (Lin's CCC=0.58). An equipercentile equating conversion from MoCA-22 to MoCA-30 was derived and externally validated across three cohorts totaling 14,375 assessments.

papers.title: Vulnerability of the Brainstem-Cerebellar Respiratory Network in Extreme Prematurity.
papers.summary: This review proposes that adverse intrauterine and extrauterine exposures (intermittent hypoxemia, inflammation, oxidative stress) during critical developmental windows in infants born <28 weeks damage the medullary serotonergic network and cerebellar fastigial nucleus. This dysmaturation is proposed to impair protective respiratory responses and mechanistically contribute to the 2-3 fold higher SUID risk in ELGANs.

papers.title: A multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with repeated experience sampling
papers.summary: This paper introduces a multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset in BIDS format from 24 healthy adults, including carbon wire loop sensors for artifact removal, continuous performance task responses, experience sampling of 13 thought dimensions, and mental health surveys across two days (~1.33 hours of simultaneous EEG-fMRI per individual). The dataset supports study of brain activity during wakeful rest and cross-session reliability of EEG-fMRI relationships.

papers.title: Improved Sleep and Clinical Outcomes Following a Single-Session Intervention among Adolescents with Borderline Personality Disorder Features
papers.summary: In this intervention trial (NCT04507308) of 57 adolescents with 3+ impairing borderline personality disorder features, a single-session sleep-focused treatment informed by the Transdiagnostic Sleep and Circadian Intervention improved objective (at-home EEG) and subjective sleep indices, with all sleep questionnaire scores improving and maintained at one-month follow-up. Multiple BPD symptom indices also improved significantly.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine-related interventions and the cGAS-STING axis in neuroinflammation: disease contexts and mechanisms of action.
papers.summary: This review organizes preclinical evidence on how traditional Chinese medicine interventions (herbal formulas, natural compounds, acupuncture, electroacupuncture) modulate the cGAS-STING axis in neuroinflammation, stratified by disease context and site of action. It reports that modulation direction is context-sensitive: pathway-related inflammation is reduced in several sterile injury models, restored STING signaling accompanies protection in acute sleep deprivation and early HSV infection, and increased STING-IFN-I signaling accompanies electroacupuncture analgesia in pain models.

papers.title: Mental replay rescales the subjective duration of past events via alpha and theta oscillations
papers.summary: Participants mentally replayed encoded naturalistic videos at compressed, expanded, or free speeds during scalp EEG; expanded replay lengthened judgments of the event's original duration while recalled gist and detail remained unaffected. Alpha and theta power were reduced under compression and interacted with speed instruction in predicting reported duration, suggesting remembered duration is reconstructed at retrieval via oscillatory dynamics rather than read out from retrieved content.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation compromises sperm quality and early embryo development by disrupting folate metabolism and DNA repair.
papers.summary: In a mouse model, sustained sleep deprivation induced germ cell apoptosis, reduced sperm motility, increased morphological abnormalities, and impaired fertilization capacity and preimplantation embryo development. Proteomics identified downregulation of the folate transporter SLC46A1 in testis and sperm, with reduced MTHFR and DNA repair proteins RAD51 and TOPBP1, and folate supplementation partially restored these proteins, linking sleep deprivation to disrupted folate metabolism and DNA repair.

papers.title: Seasonal Variation in Mood and Associated Patterns of Sleep, Activity, Circadian Rhythms and Light.
papers.summary: In 733 wrist-actigraphy observation periods from 422 young Australians with emerging mood disorders, depressive and negative symptoms peaked in winter while manic symptoms peaked in autumn. Winter increases in negative symptoms were indirectly associated with an 'extended sleep with phase-delayed activity' profile and a constrained moderate-to-bright indoor light exposure pattern, and winter depressive symptoms with lower physical activity.

papers.title: EEG-Based Cognitive Overload-Driven Adaptive Training for Enhancing Performance Under Simulated High-Stress Space Operation Tasks.
papers.summary: Developed an EEG-based cognitive overload-driven adaptive training system combining hybrid feature selection, NFDTW feature alignment, and a dual-factor task regulation strategy. Online overload detection reached 92.07% and 84.67% accuracy on two datasets, and the adaptive group showed significantly improved task performance and stress/anxiety scores in a VR robotic arm docking task.

papers.title: EEG Feature-level integration for robust command generation in SSVEP-based brain-computer interfaces.
papers.summary: The study exploited the SSVEP Blocking Response (attenuation/disappearance of SSVEP) as an additional controllable neural signal for command generation in SSVEP-based BCIs, using a detection method based on alpha rhythm sensitivity during state transitions and an EEG feature-level integration strategy. The method improved SSVEP-BR detection over the prior framework by 17.11% precision, 8.50% recall, and 5.44% specificity offline, and an asynchronous system achieved 8-command robotic arm control using only two stimulation frequencies in 5 online subjects.

papers.title: Outcome-Blind EEG Microstate Topography After Cardiac Arrest: Spatial Expression of a Lateralized Microstate and Association with Neurological Outcome.
papers.summary: In a secondary analysis of the multicenter I-CARE/PhysioNet database (567 comatose cardiac arrest survivors), outcome-blind EEG microstate decomposition identified a frozen four-state solution in which M2 global explained variance was higher in patients with favorable neurological outcome (median 0.0852 vs 0.0564) and inversely associated with CPC severity. M2 GEV remained associated with favorable outcome after adjustment (OR 1.30 per SD; OR 1.47 in the ROSC-adjusted model), though standalone discrimination was modest (AUC 0.59).

papers.title: Personal nighttime indoor temperature and sleep characteristics in adults with type 2 diabetes.
papers.summary: Using repeated-night data from 108 adults with type 2 diabetes (1307 paired sleep-temperature nights), this study examined associations between personal nighttime indoor temperature and actigraphy-derived sleep. Warmer-than-usual nights were associated with higher sleep efficiency and fewer awakenings in within-person linear models, and generalized additive models showed nonlinear associations with sleep efficiency, wake after sleep onset, and awakenings, with model-predicted benefits emerging above approximately 27 °C but based on sparse upper-range observations.

papers.title: The moderating role of anger rumination and self-control in the day-to-day associations between irritability and sleep in male adolescents: An exploratory experience sampling method study.
papers.summary: A 9-day experience sampling study in 56 male adolescents found that poorer sleep quality predicted higher next-day irritability, and that daily anger rumination and self-control directly predicted next-day irritability, with sleep-irritability associations moderated by between-person rumination and self-control; lower irritability also predicted better subsequent sleep quality.

papers.title: Depth-adaptive suppression of subject-dependent interference for robust cross-subject EEG emotion recognition.
papers.summary: Proposes a two-stage, layer-adaptive subject-interference suppression framework built on EEG Conformer for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition, using differentiable gates and adversarial subject classifiers to locate subject-informative layers plus a subject-aware supervised contrastive regularizer. Under leave-one-subject-out evaluation on SEED it outperformed representative machine-learning, domain-adaptation, and deep-learning baselines, with auxiliary adaptability on SEED-IV and layer-wise probing showing subject information is strongest in shallow and early intermediate representations.

papers.title: E-MDD: an evidence-guided explainable framework for EEG-based depression recognition.
papers.summary: Develops E-MDD, an evidence-guided explainable framework that fuses EEG latent features with neurophysiological biomarkers via parallel branches and a lightweight MLP for depression recognition, then constructs structured evidence aligned to biomarkers to guide a large language model in generating faithful textual explanations. On the Mumtaz dataset it achieved an AUC of 0.8472 and F1-score of 0.8421, with consistent evidence-guided explanation performance across EEGNet and EEGConformer.

papers.title: Nocturnal sleep duration, clinical activity score, and thyroid functional remission after radioactive iodine therapy in Graves' disease with thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy.
papers.summary: Retrospective single-center cohort of 153 patients with Graves' disease and thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy examined whether pretreatment nocturnal sleep duration and Clinical Activity Score predict thyroid functional remission after radioactive iodine therapy. Longer sleep (OR 6.13 per hour) and lower CAS (OR 0.64 per point) were associated with remission in post-selection models, and no patient sleeping under 6 h achieved remission, but the authors describe these threshold effects as exploratory and requiring prospective validation.

papers.title: Functional brain activity in cancer-related cognitive impairment: a scoping review of EEG studies.
papers.summary: Scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidance that mapped 60 EEG studies of cognitive functioning in people with cancer, characterizing populations, paradigms, and cognitive outcomes. Task-based event-related potentials (oddball and attention tasks) predominated over quantitative EEG; longer P300 latency and lower amplitude were common outside CNS cancers but findings were inconsistent, and EEG-cognition associations were rarely tested directly.

papers.title: Psychological support for depression and anxiety across chronic illness contexts: a comparative evaluation of three general-purpose AI chatbots.
papers.summary: Standardized simulated-patient benchmarking study comparing ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao on 20 depression/anxiety scenarios across type 2 diabetes and chronic spontaneous urticaria, yielding 120 blinded-rated responses. Overall appropriateness differed across systems (90.0% ChatGPT, 75.0% Gemini, 55.0% Doubao meeting threshold), performance dropped for moderate presentations (58.3% appropriate) and CSU contextualization, and major safety errors occurred in 0%, 10.0%, and 15.0% of first-round responses respectively.

papers.title: Autonomy satisfaction and bedtime procrastination among generation Z university students: The serial mediating roles of general self-efficacy and AI dependence.
papers.summary: Using a cross-sectional survey of 717 Chinese Generation Z university students and structural equation modeling with bootstrap mediation, the study tested whether general self-efficacy and AI dependence serially mediate the association between autonomy satisfaction and bedtime procrastination. Autonomy satisfaction was negatively associated with AI dependence and bedtime procrastination, and both mediators were significant, with AI dependence accounting for the larger indirect effect.

papers.title: The Moderating Effect of Sleep Duration on the Association Between Chronic Disease and Health-Related Quality of Life in Middle-Aged Women.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional secondary analysis of 3062 middle-aged Korean women from the 2019 and 2021 KNHANES examined whether sleep duration moderates the association between number of chronic diseases and health-related quality of life. More chronic diseases were associated with lower HRQOL, and this negative association was stronger among women sleeping more than 9 h/day than in the 6-7 h/day reference group.

papers.title: Network analysis of frailty, sleep quality, and life satisfaction in older patients: a cross-sectional study stratified by chronic disease burden.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional network analysis of 1,107 older patients (97.4% with multimorbidity), life satisfaction nodes showed high strength and bridge centrality, sleep-related nodes (sleep latency, sleeping medication use, daytime dysfunction) were prominent in centrality indices, and frailty nodes connected to life satisfaction mainly through negative edges; negative cross-community connections appeared more pronounced in those with ≥5 chronic diseases, though between-group differences were descriptive.

papers.title: EEG decodability of facial expressions and their stereoscopic depth cues in immersive virtual reality
papers.summary: Combining immersive virtual reality, EEG, and eye tracking in 34 participants, the study used time-resolved multivariate decoding to examine neural representation of facial expressions under monoscopic versus stereoscopic depth conditions. EEG reliably differentiated expressions, stereoscopic depth cues produced a distinct decodable neural signature, and expression decoding remained robust across depth conditions, while gaze patterns carried comparable expression information but did not account for the neural representations.

papers.title: Case Report: Smith-Magenis syndrome with bilateral high-grade vesicoureteral reflux, hypothyroidism, and seizure in infancy.
papers.summary: A 9-month-old boy with recurrent febrile urinary tract infection, bilateral high-grade vesicoureteral reflux, hypothyroidism, global developmental delay, and dysmorphic features was diagnosed with Smith-Magenis syndrome via trio whole-exome sequencing identifying a de novo 3.63-Mb 17p11.2 deletion encompassing RAI1; management included antibiotics, levothyroxine, and antibiotic prophylaxis, with improved renal indices and no recurrent urinary tract infection at follow-up.

papers.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes with High-Volume Hemodiafiltration Versus High-Flux Hemodialysis Across Clinical Subgroups: Results from the CONVINCE Trial.
papers.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
papers.summary: This prespecified exploratory subgroup analysis of the CONVINCE randomized trial (1211 participants with PRO assessments) found broadly consistent patient-reported outcome effects of high-volume hemodiafiltration versus high-flux hemodialysis across clinical subgroups, with only modest, unadjusted nominal interactions (e.g., dialysis vintage with physical function, age with pain interference) and no convincing clinically meaningful treatment-effect heterogeneity.

papers.title: Association between lactic dehydrogenase-to-albumin ratio and all-cause mortality in critical obstructive sleep apnea patients: a retrospective cohort study from the MIMIC-IV database.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 1,118 critically ill obstructive sleep apnea patients from MIMIC-IV, higher lactate dehydrogenase-to-albumin ratio (LDAR) was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality at 30 days, 90 days, 180 days, and 1 year, with a positive linear relationship and a 139.8% higher 90-day mortality risk in the highest versus lowest LDAR quartile.

papers.title: A systematic review of economic evaluations of strategies to diagnose obstructive sleep apnoea in adults.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 29 economic evaluations of diagnostic strategies for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea found substantial methodological heterogeneity in diagnostic thresholds, model structures, and assumptions about CPAP adherence, with only four studies using home respiratory polygraphy as a comparator, limiting applicability to the UK setting and leaving the true cost-effectiveness of contemporary diagnostic pathways uncertain.

papers.title: "It Just Puts You Out!" Tranq Sleep, Sensory Discernment, and the Experience of Consuming Xylazine-Adulterated Fentanyl in Rural North Carolina
papers.summary: Twenty-five in-depth qualitative interviews with fentanyl consumers in rural west-central North Carolina documented sensory discernment strategies for detecting xylazine adulteration (residue appearance on foil, bitterness and chemical odor when smoked, altered viscosity when injected) and a distinctive involuntary sedation termed 'tranq sleep,' distinct from opioid nod and followed by severe withdrawal. Findings extend the xylazine literature geographically and pharmacologically and highlight harm reduction needs.

papers.title: The impact of menstruation-related symptoms on women's quality of life, work productivity, and economic burden: a structured narrative review.
papers.summary: Structured narrative review of 86 studies (2014-2025) examining how dysmenorrhoea, PMS/PMDD, and HMB/AUB affect quality of life, work productivity, and economic burden. Menstruation-related disorders were consistently associated with reduced health-related QOL and productivity loss driven predominantly by presenteeism rather than absenteeism, with psychological distress as a key contributor.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
